conditionalAward.formulaText: For a responsive and selected MDOT NEVI Round 3 proposal, conditional_award_cents should be modeled as Total Funds Requested from Form 3 or the accepted Revised Price Proposal, capped at floor(0.80 * MDOT-approved Total Eligible Cost). If Total Funds Requested is unavailable pre-award, use floor(0.80 * eligible_project_cost_cents) only for internal modeling after application fit, site/equipment compliance, timely proposal submission, current funding/open status, and at least 20% Project Company Share are confirmed. If a project is selected and MDOT has accepted an award, executed contract, or accepted Revised Price Proposal amount, use approved_total_funds_requested_cents as the deterministic post-award reimbursement/payment value subject to contract terms, milestone/payment conditions, change orders, withholding, and deductions.
calculationTrace: MDOT Round 3 is an active competitive DBOM procurement; the official project page lists RFP issuance on 2026-06-08, proposals due 2026-08-07, and anticipated award in October 2026.
RFP Section 1.3 says MDOT will award, if at all, to responsive and responsible proposers offering the Best Value Proposal and reserves the right to reject any or all proposals.

The price proposal instructions require itemized eligible costs only; Form 3 requires a minimum 20% Project Company Share and shows Total Funds Requested as Total Eligible Cost less Project Company Share with a maximum 80% share.

If all pre-award gating inputs are present, internal expected_value_cents may be modeled as floor(conditional_award_cents * 0.38), but it should remain excluded from default user-facing totals until selected or contract-executed status and an approved amount are present.

Therefore no source-backed dollar value can be calculated for the matched project until site-specific eligible costs and proposal/award inputs are known; there is no per-project dollar cap found beyond the 80% cost-share cap and approved Total Funds Requested mechanics.

probabilityEvidence.probabilityNotes: Michigan-specific historical evidence exists: the FY 2026 Michigan EVID Plan reports 83 project sites selected from 214 submitted proposals across the first two competitive NEVI procurement rounds. The conservative discount is floor_to_two_decimals(83 / 214) = 0.38. Round 3 remains project-specific and competitive; its actual application count is not yet known, so this is a historical prior rather than a project-level probability. MDOT's Round 3 press release states that about $51 million remains and anticipates about 60 additional stations, but that budget/expected-awards evidence is not enough to replace the historical application denominator.

fallbackPriorSuggestion.basis: Fallback prior not needed because Michigan-specific historical selection evidence was found. Do not use any fallback prior without human approval for projects that lack eligible project cost, application-fit review, and proposal/award status.

conditionalAward.formulaText: For a selected and formally approved GFO-25-603 project only, calculate conditional reimbursement as min(cec_approved_award_amount_cents, requested_grant_amount_cents, round(0.80 * eligible_project_cost_cents), solicitation_applicant_award_cap_cents). For GFO-25-603, the current solicitation-specific applicant cap is 35% of $79,000,000 available funding, or $27,650,000. Exact payable reimbursement also depends on eligible invoiced costs, match compliance, CEC approval/agreement status, and required FHWA/Caltrans authorization for the relevant phase.
calculationTrace: CEC's official GFO-25-603 page lists the solicitation as Active, with release date February 23, 2026, submission deadline October 16, 2026 at 11:59 pm, and questions deadline July 13, 2026 at 5:00 pm.

CEC describes GFO-25-603 as a competitive grant solicitation with up to $79,000,000 available for publicly accessible high-powered DC fast charging stations supporting light-duty EV travel along major corridors.
CEC workshop materials state that total available funding is $79,000,000 and that the maximum grant award per applicant is 35% of funds available, equal to $27,650,000.
Federal NEVI cost share is capped at 80% of total project cost, so the project must supply the remaining non-federal share.
Before selection/approval, there is no source-backed project-specific award amount; the source-backed value is a conditional formula and cap, not an entitlement.

probabilityEvidence.probabilityNotes: Official sources confirm a competitive solicitation with screening, scoring, ranking by cost-per-CCS-port, and funding until solicitation funds are exhausted. They do not provide a current GFO-25-603 application denominator, expected award count, or success-rate history suitable for an award-probability discount. Available funding, the 80% cost-share limit, and the $27.65 million applicant cap are conditional cap information, not probability evidence.

fallbackPriorSuggestion.basis: Only a human-reviewed prior should be used for this competitive NEVI solicitation unless RetroFi obtains an official application denominator, expected award count, award-count history, or an approved internal prior for comparable CEC NEVI rounds.

calculationTrace: CEC lists GFO-25-603 as an active competitive grant solicitation with up to $79,000,000 available and an October 16, 2026 application deadline.
The current applicant cap is 35% of total solicitation funds; 35% of $79,000,000 is $27,650,000, or 2765000000 cents.

The solicitation requires exactly 20% match share of total allowable project cost, implying a maximum 80% reimbursable share for a compliant budget; at least 50% of the match share must be cash match.
Eligible reimbursable/match costs depend on project phase authorization, executed grant agreement, allowable-cost rules, site eligibility, equipment requirements, and documentation.
Applications must pass screening and minimum technical scoring thresholds, then are ranked by cost per CCS port; CEC may recommend partial funding if remaining funds are insufficient.

The Notice of Proposed Awards is expected after the application deadline and will contain the proposed funding amount, rank order, and proposed award amounts; no project-specific GFO-25-603 award record was found before that official decision.

probabilityEvidence.probabilityNotes: Official sources provide a competitive scored process, minimum score thresholds, cost-per-CCS-port ranking, total budget, applicant cap, and anticipated NOPA timing, but they do not provide GFO-25-603 application volume, expected award count, a historical success rate, or any official probability discount. The $79,000,000 budget and $27,650,000 applicant cap are capacity/cap inputs, not selection probability evidence. Cost-per-CCS-port ranking is project-specific and cannot be converted to a conservative award probability without applicant pool and ranking data.

repairs.programName: GFO-25-605 - Reliable Electric Charging for Eligible School-bus Sites (RECESS)

conditionalAward.formulaText: Use the approved award amount from a CEC Notice of Proposed Awards, Business Meeting approval, or fully executed agreement when available. Before an award decision, the current Addendum 2 conditional maximum is: min(eligible_project_cost_cents, 2,000,000 cents x eligible L2 charging ports + 3,750,000 cents x eligible DCFC or bidirectional DCFC charging ports, applicable lane cap). Lane 1 has no fixed dollar applicant cap in the current source; it is constrained by the Table 4 maximum number of charging ports for the eligible LEA and by demonstrated electric school bus charging need. Lane 2 cap is 225,000,000 cents. Lane 3 cap is 225,000,000 cents when serving one LEA and 450,000,000 cents when serving more than one LEA. Total requested grid-connected charging ports cannot exceed demonstrated electric school bus need. A dual-port DCFC or bidirectional DCFC equals two eligible DCFC/bidirectional DCFC ports, so it maps to 7,500,000 cents if both ports are eligible.
calculationTrace: Official CEC page lists GFO-25-605 as active with submission deadline August 31, 2026 at 11:59 pm and up to 2,200,000,000 cents available for electric school bus EV charging infrastructure.
Official CEC page and Addendum 2 split funding into Lane 1 first-come with 400,000,000 cents, Lane 2 competitive with 900,000,000 cents, and Lane 3 competitive with 900,000,000 cents.

Current Addendum 2 changed the DCFC/bidirectional DCFC model to a per-port award: L2 charging port = 2,000,000 cents; DCFC or bidirectional DCFC port = 3,750,000 cents. Retain 7,500,000 cents only as the equivalent of two eligible DCFC/bidirectional DCFC ports.

Current Addendum 2 sets single applicant caps: Lane 1 up to the Table 4/HVIP-related maximum charging port count; Lane 2 225,000,000 cents; Lane 3 225,000,000 cents for one LEA or 450,000,000 cents for more than one LEA.
Addendum 2 and Q&A state that costs incurred before agreement execution are ineligible and that funds are disbursed as reimbursement for eligible incurred costs supported by invoices.

CEC may partially fund proposals, modify scope/funding, cancel awards, and no agreement is effective until CEC approval and signatures; therefore the formula is a conditional maximum unless an approved/executed award amount is known.

probabilityEvidence.probabilityNotes: No single defensible award probability exists for this mixed-lane opportunity. Lane 1 is not a competitive probability problem once the project is a Table 4 eligible LEA, the application is complete and timely, and it passes screening; the official Q&A says funding for the maximum number of charging ports per eligible Lane 1 applicant has been reserved if a complete application is received before the deadline. However, that does not supply a generic probability for non-confirmed applicants. Lanes 2 and 3 are competitive: applications must pass screening, score at least 70 percent overall and 70 percent on Project Implementation and Readiness, then are ranked until lane funds are exhausted. No official historical applications denominator, success rate, expected application count, expected award count, or current NOPA/award list was found for Lanes 2 and 3.

fallbackPriorSuggestion.basis: Do not use a generic prior. For Lane 1, use no probability discount only after confirming the applicant is Table 4 eligible, the application is complete/timely, and the project passes screening or has a proposed/approved award. For Lanes 2 and 3, any fallback probability would be a human-reviewed prior because only budget, scoring criteria, and ranked-until-funds-exhausted rules were found.

calculationTrace: Colorado Energy Office current page identifies this as the Direct Current Fast-Charging Plazas Grant, with eligible applicant categories, NEVI and CAE funding sources, $17 million funding amount, match varying up to 80%, and application round labeled Spring 2026.

Colorado Energy Office current page states incentives are available per charging port, require a minimum of four charging ports, require minimum 150 kW output per port, depend on the number of vehicles that can be charged at 150 kW at one time, and vary by location.

The same official page defers detailed incentive amounts to the DCFC Plazas Application Guide. That Google Drive guide opened only as a loading/sign-in page through extraction, so the current-round rate table, location rows, storage adders, eligible-cost definitions, and per-site caps were not machine-extracted.

CDOT confirms NEVI funds are distributed through CEO's DCFC Plazas Program and states NEVI-funded projects must be within one mile of a federally designated Alternative Fuel Corridor, while CAE funding makes all parts of Colorado eligible under the DCFC Plazas Program.
